summary: Flattrade's om order updates: an intraday order open, partly filled and complete, one rejected with the RMS text, and an NFO stop-loss order cancelled.

notes: Flattrade's order updates ride the market data socket as om frames after {"t":"o"}, on the web since 73599f37c (marketcalls/openalgo#2507, issue #2386) and on the desktop: the web's market data adapter relays each om frame verbatim to its order adapter, which normalises it (normalize_order_frame).

Where the two send t=o on that socket differs. The desktop sends it after PiConnect's login acknowledgement (ak), with its other post-login frames (NorenFeed::on_authenticated), the handshake Flattrade documents (09-websocket.md: connect, wait for the ak, then t=o, as quoted in flattrade_order_adapter.py's module docs) and the order the web's own order socket keeps (FlattradeOrderUpdateAdapter sends t=o on the ak). The web's market data adapter sends it from its on_open callback (FlattradeWebSocketAdapter._on_open: _resubscribe_all, then _subscribe_order_updates), which flattrade_websocket.py calls right after the t=a login frame, before the ak. New with 73599f37c: until then the web's only t=o went out on its order socket, after the ak. The cases here script the desktop's order (t=o after the ak push); the web replay sends no upstream frames to compare.
The order book is served empty: the order catch-up's first read, at the login, only records it.
